title: A Dust Storm Swallowed a Quarter of Mars and Killed a NASA Rover

scenes.text: A dust storm swallowed a quarter of Mars and killed a robot.
June 2018. A storm grows bigger than North America in days, then wraps the whole planet.
The sky goes black. The Opportunity rover runs on solar panels.
It had been built to last 90 days. It had driven 28 miles over 14 years.
Its last message: my battery is low and it's getting dark. Then silence.
NASA sent over 1,000 wake-up calls for eight months. Nothing. A storm the size of a planet.

description:
In June 2018 a dust storm on Mars grew from larger than North America to a quarter of the planet, then encircled it, blocking almost all sunlight.
NASA's solar-powered Opportunity rover, designed for 90 days and 1,000 metres, had lasted nearly 15 years and driven more than 28 miles. Its last signal came on 10 June 2018; after more than 1,000 recovery commands, NASA declared the mission over in February 2019.
Would you send a robot to Mars that could die alone? Comment below.
thumbnail_text: A STORM KILLED A NASA ROVER
first_comment: Opportunity's famous last words were a journalist's translation of its final data readings, but the numbers were real: battery low, sky almost black. Which rover would you want to bring home?
